messages:
alice: Hey — saw a regression in continuous-batching after yesterday's routing tweak. P95 latency up ~15% for short chats. From quick traces it looks like a lot of single-request batches when requests hit mixed-variant compat sets (A vs B).

alice: pasted logs and a tiny repro:
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] request id=rx1 model=A variant=v1 routing=hash->A
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] request id=rx2 model=A variant=v2 routing=fallback->v1 (compat mismatch)
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] batch formed size=1 reason=compat_incompatibility
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] kvcache miss for rx2 warmup=0
```

alice: attaching pprof link (internal) and short perf counters — seems that kernel selection for v2 is picking slower int8 path for <=32 tokens which pushes per-token time high and batching timer fires.

ben: Can you drop the exact batcher config used? especially token_budget_target and queue_policy timeouts. might be the budget too low for mixed-variant traffic.

alice: config is default continuous batching: token_budget_target=32, max_batch_size=128, queue_max_latency_ms=18, compat_grouping=true.

chris: hmm. two things: (1) KV warmup: v2 cold KV causes first few tokens to be ~2-3x slower; (2) kernel sel: our int8 kernel has a worse startup cost for short seqs -> increases latency variance. When compat_grouping=true and routing mixes variants, the batcher often waits only queue_max_latency_ms and emits tiny batches.

chris: idea: add a transient "variant_warmup_grace_ms" when a model-variant pair hasn't had a recent token in KV for X ms; hold batch formation for that id for up to N ms to let warmup requests accumulate.

alice: that could help, but careful with throughput — we don't want to globally stall. Maybe scope warmup grace to rare variants (low qps) only.

dina: alternative: change token_budget_target to be token-budget-per-compat-set instead of per-request. If compat set mixes variants, increase the target to favor larger batches. Eg token_budget_target_per_compat=48 for mixed sets.

ben: +1 to per-compat budgeting. Also we could relax compat_grouping for a short window: if a variant is compatible but imposes >1.8x per-token cost, allow batching together and add a per-request fallback policy that re-routes slow ones after N tokens. That trades accuracy for latency but might be OK for best-effort routes.

eric: I ran a quick local loadgen with a 60/40 mix (v1/v2) hitting model=A. Results:
- default: median batch size=3, 27% singletons, P95 latency +18%
- token_budget_target=48: median batch size=6, singletons -> 12%, p95 -6% vs default
- variant_warmup_grace_ms=50 (for low-qps variants): median batch size=5, singletons 9%, p95 -9%

eric: command I used:
```sh
./loadgen --model A --mix 0.6,0.4 --seq-len-dist short --duration 300 \ 
  --batcher.token_budget_target=48 --batcher.queue_max_latency_ms=18
```

eric: attaching csv of runs to the CI artifact (link).

alice: nice. Any downsides observed (mem, latency tail for warmed variants)?

eric: small increase in average latency for the warm variant by ~2ms, memory +3% (batches larger). No OOMs.

chris: sounds promising. Ops-wise: implement token_budget per-compat-set and a heuristic for small warmup_grace for low-qps variants. Also log a metric: compat_singleton_rate and compat_mixed_batch_penalty (P95 delta).

dina: I'll own the batching config change PR (small toggle behind feature flag). Will add tests: synthetic mixed-variant workloads and a canary against prod traffic.

alice: great. Action items:
- dina: PR for per-compat token_budget + feature flag (owner dina)
- chris: prototype variant_warmup_grace_ms heuristic and add metrics (owner chris)
- ben: review kernel selection heuristics for short sequences (owner ben)
- eric: run expanded load tests across more mixes and seq-length distributions (owner eric)

ci-bot: deploy queued: batching-config-flag -> staging (build #5421). :rocket:

alice: will follow up tomorrow with prod canary thresholds. thanks all :thumbsup:
